title: Quartiles, interquartile range (IQR) and the boxplot

videos.script: The median cut the deliveries in half. Now cut each half in half again. {{halves}} You get three cut points. A quarter of the deliveries are faster than the first. Half are faster than the second, which is the median. Three quarters are faster than the third. These are the quartiles. {{quartiles}} The distance between the first and the third is the interquartile range. It is the width of the middle half of the data, and like the median, one wild value cannot move it. {{iqr}} Now draw it. A box from the first quartile to the third. A line inside it at the median. A whisker out to each side. And any delivery too far from the box drawn on its own, as a dot. {{box}} That is a boxplot. It fits five numbers and the odd outlier into a strip you can read in a second. {{strip}} Its real strength appears when you put several side by side. Four neighbourhoods, four boxes, one scale. You can see at a glance which is slowest and which is least predictable. {{side}}
